device.description: 16-bit 100 kSPS 8-channel SAR ADC with start-bit serial interface
device.note: ads8344.pdf (SBAS139E) p.2 pin configuration and descriptions, p.3-4 electrical characteristics (+VCC 4.75-5.25 V / 2.7-3.6 V, VIH to 5.5 V, straight binary), p.11 Tables I-II channel selection, p.12 digital interface (inputs 5.5 V tolerant, Figure 3), p.13 Tables III-V control byte and clock modes, Figure 4, p.14 internal clock mode, Table VI timing, Figures 5-6

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: internal: the last control byte (S A2 A1 A0 - SGL/DIF PD1 PD0); no read-back, reset value not documented

registers.name: CLKMODE
registers.note: internal: the clock mode the part keeps (Table V): 1 = internal clock (PD1-PD0 = 10), 0 = external clock (PD1-PD0 = 11); PD1-PD0 = 00 keeps the previous mode. The datasheet leaves the power-on mode undefined (the user must set it); the model starts in external clock mode

commands.name: Control Byte (internal clock mode)
commands.note: Tables III-V, Figures 3-6: S A2 A1 A0 - SGL/DIF PD1 PD0 (bit 3 unused); after the byte DOUT is low for one clock, then D15..D0 MSB first, then zeros. A2-A0 = 000/100/001/101/010/110/011/111 give +IN = CH0..CH7 in both SGL/DIF modes. PD1-PD0 = 10 selects internal clock mode

commands.name: Control Byte (external clock mode)
commands.note: PD1-PD0 = 11: no power-down, external clock mode

commands.name: Control Byte (reserved PD1-PD0 = 01)
commands.note: PD1-PD0 = 01 is reserved (Table V); treated as external clock mode

commands.name: Control Byte (power-down between conversions)
commands.note: PD1-PD0 = 00: power-down between conversions, the clock mode stays as it was

commands.name: Idle (no start bit)
commands.note: DIN is ignored until the start bit (the first HIGH bit after CS falls)

pages: p.2 (pins, ordering: E = QSOP-20 DBQ, N = SSOP-20 DB), p.3-4 (specs), p.11 (Tables I-II), p.12 (digital interface, Figure 3), p.13 (Tables III-V, Figure 4), p.14 (clock modes, Table VI, Figures 5-6)
notModeled: analog inputs, multiplexer and SGL/DIF selection (stored only); every conversion returns the 0 V code 0000h

external clock mode: the conversion is clocked by DCLK (16 clocks after the control byte); not timed, the result is ready at once; BUSY is a one-DCLK HIGH pulse after the control byte on the part, the model only drives it LOW

internal clock mode: BUSY low for up to 8 us (modeled as an 8 us conversion); the part shifts the MSB on the first DCLK falling edge after BUSY rises, the model shifts the reply right after the control byte (the 0 V code is all zeros either way); reading after CS was high during the conversion is not modeled separately
a clock-mode change needs one extra conversion cycle on the part; the model switches with the control byte that selects it
DOUT and BUSY are Hi-Z while CS is high (the bus model floats DOUT; BUSY is driven), except BUSY in internal clock mode
power-down selection PD1-PD0 = 00 (auto power-down between conversions has no bus effect)
overlapped 24-clock conversions where the next start bit arrives while the previous result is still shifting (Figure 3): the model restarts the reply at the new control byte
timing values are the 2.7-3.6 V table (Table VI, 200 ns); at 4.75-5.25 V they are 70-100 ns (Table VII)
variants: ADS8345 (ads8345.pdf) is the bipolar twos-complement version with the same pinout and interface; ADS8341/ADS8343 are the 4-channel 16-pin versions; ADS7844 the 12-bit version.
